catalog_quote: The basic syllable pattern is (C)V(V)(V). Syllables are either short or long, each having variant tone patterns. Short syllables are distinguished from long syllables strictly on the basis of timing. A short syllable has one unit (mora) of timing and a long syllable has two. The domain of accent is the syllable as a whole. This means that even for long syllables (two moras of timing) the accent is born by the entire unit rather than just one or the other of the vowel segments. In this paper accent is only specified for certain contexts that distinguish similar tense-aspect forms (e.g. -g IMMEDIATE and -'g RECENT PAST 2). Auye has 2 emic tones (high and low) and would probably be classified as a reduced word-tone system (contrasting on only one syllable per word) according to Donohue (1997). Besides indicating the placement of the accented syllable, the lexicon also identifies the tone assigned to the word as a whole. The assigned tone (high or low) is realized at the beginning of the word (or noun phrase) and is sustained over each succeeding syllable until the accented one is reached, after which the pitch falls gradually from high to low word-finally. In this paper tone is only indicated on the low tone word mèe ‘person, man’ to distinguish it from the high tone word mee DEM.SG.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Each word has one accented syllable whose position is lexically specified (not predictable by rule; certain verbal suffixes are inherently accented, e.g. -'ta FAR PAST, -'p RECENT PAST, -'g RECENT PAST 2, contrasting with unaccented -g IMMEDIATE), plus a lexical word tone (H or L) that is held from the word/NP onset up to the accented syllable, after which pitch falls to low at the word end. The author classes this as a two-tone 'reduced word-tone system' (Donohue 1997), i.e. a culminative tonal/pitch accent system rather than stress.
new_statements.exceptions: The plural-action suffix -taa DURATIVE and the auxiliary ta/se 'do' never take accent; accent alone distinguishes -g IMMEDIATE from -'g RECENT PAST 2. In the paper accent and tone are otherwise left unmarked (tone written only on mèe 'person' vs mee DEM.SG).
new_statements.domain_note: Accent domain is the syllable (whole long syllable, not a single mora); one accent per word; the lexical tone is realized over the word or the noun phrase. Statement is a brief phonology endnote in a discourse paper by the SIL field linguist (first-hand), not a full phonology chapter; the fuller treatment is in the unpublished Moxness 2003 grammar Ms.
new_statements.identity_note: The source describes Auye proper [auu] = auye1238 (c. 500 speakers north of the Mee/Ekari and Wodani areas, east of Nabire), not the Dao/Moi-Wadea [daz] variety that Wikipedia lumps with it as 'Auye-Dao' (Glottolog parent auye1239). The earlier scan's 'Tebay, Soren E. 2019' reference does not appear in Glottolog's lists for auye1238 or auye1239 and could not be verified.

sources.locator: Endnote 1, p. 42 (PDF p. 43); accent-marked suffix paradigm in table (38), p. 23, and remark on unaccented -taa / ta/se, pp. 30-31
sources.note: Endnote 1 (p. 42): Auye has a lexically placed 'accent' (domain = the syllable, one accented syllable per word) plus 2 emic word-level tones (H/L); the lexical tone is realized from the start of the word up to the accented syllable, after which pitch falls to low word-finally; author calls it a 'reduced word-tone system' after Donohue 1997. Accent is marked with an apostrophe on certain tense-aspect suffixes (-'ta FAR PAST, -'p RECENT PAST, -'g RECENT PAST 2 vs unaccented -g IMMEDIATE); -taa DUR and auxiliary ta/se never take accent (p. 30-31). No use of the word 'stress'.
